title: NariQ releases 3-bit Qwen3.8-27B GGUF claiming near-BF16 quality
summary: NariQ has released 3-bit-or-lower GGUF quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B for local inference, including a 10 GB file it says retains near-BF16 quality across agentic, math, multilingual, and image-understanding tasks; running them currently requires NariQ&\#x27;s llama.cpp fork. In NariQ&\#x27;s self-reported benchmarks, the 3-bit and 2.5-bit versions are roughly at BF16 parity on several tests—Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores 63.8 and 60.2 versus 62.6 for BF16, and AIME 25+26 scores 98.3 and 96.5 versus 97.7—while the 2-bit version drops to 52.4 and 86.0. NariQ reports decode speed comparable to other quants on an RTX PRO 6000.
